text:
Fixed. `src/plugin/timezone/index.js`: `dayjs.tz(input, timezone)` treated every input as a local wall-clock string, so a timestamp, JS `Date`, or Day.js object was reinterpreted as wall time in the target zone instead of being treated as an absolute instant and converted (e.g. `dayjs.tz(1401638400000, 'America/New_York')` gave `2014-06-01T16:00:00-04:00` instead of `2014-06-01T12:00:00-04:00`).

Change: when `input` is not a string, delegate to `d(input).tz(timezone)` (instant → target zone); string input keeps the existing wall-time-in-zone parsing path. Verified all three input kinds now match moment-timezone for format/valueOf/utcOffset, DST boundaries still behave, and the full suite is 524/524 green (same pre-existing TZ-specific failures before and after, none introduced).

Fixed. `src/locale/nl.js`: the Dutch `ordinal` returned `${n}.` (German-style), so `Do` produced `1.`/`2.`/`8.` instead of the Dutch forms moment produces (`1ste`, `2de`, `8ste`, `20ste`, ...).

Change: `ordinal: n => `[${n}${(n === 1 || n === 8 || n >= 20) ? 'ste' : 'de'}]``. The square brackets are required because `ordinal`'s output is fed back through `format`, and the letters in `ste`/`de` (`s`, `d`) are format tokens — without brackets `1ste` formats to `10te`. This matches the convention already used by `sv`, `en-gb`, etc.

Verified: `dayjs(d).locale('nl').format('Do')` now equals `moment(d).locale('nl').format('Do')` for all days 1–31, and `dddd Do MMMM` matches too. Full suite 524/524 green, and the TZ-specific pre-existing failures are byte-identical to baseline.
Done. I had not started request #4, so `src/plugin/weekYear/index.js` was never modified and is untouched (`git diff` shows no change to it). Nothing to undo.

Fixed. `src/plugin/timezone/index.js`, `proto.tz`: the offset was derived from `toLocaleString` output, which has no milliseconds, so for any input with sub-second precision `diff` came out fractional and the offset became e.g. `-420.00205` — making `format('Z')` return `-07:0.0020499999999969987` instead of `-07:00`.

Change:
```js
const offset = localUtcOffset - Math.round(diff)
return d(this.valueOf()).utcOffset(offset)
```
`Math.round` recovers the exact whole-minute offset (the fractional part is always the sub-second remainder), and building from `this.valueOf()` keeps the exact instant, so milliseconds are no longer dropped.

Verified against moment-timezone across 13 zones × ms ∈ {0,1,123,500,999} plus a MockDate-pinned `dayjs()`: `format('Z')`, `format()`, `valueOf()` and `utcOffset()` all match. Whole-second inputs are unchanged, full suite 524/524 green, TZ-specific pre-existing failures byte-identical to baseline.

Undone. `d.tz` in `src/plugin/timezone/index.js` is back to its original form (no `typeof input !== 'string'` branch); only the separate `proto.tz` fix from request #2 remains in that file. Verified the original behaviour is restored.

Fixed. `src/plugin/customParseFormat/index.js` hard-coded English meridiem handling: the `A`/`a` tokens used the fixed regexes `/[AP]M/` and `/[ap]m/` and set `afternoon` by comparing to the literal `'PM'`/`'pm'`. So any locale whose `meridiem()` returns non-English strings could never be parsed — e.g. `dayjs('2018-05-02 12:00 午後', 'YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm A', 'ja')` returned Invalid Date while moment returned a valid date.

Changes:
- Added `meridiemMatch(input, isLowerCase)` which, when the active locale defines `meridiem`, finds the hour whose `meridiem(hour, 0, isLowerCase)` string matches the input and treats hour >= 12 as PM; otherwise falls back to the English comparison.
- Added `getMeridiemRegex(isLowerCase)` which builds the token regex from the locale's distinct `meridiem()` outputs (falling back to the English regexes when the locale has no `meridiem`), and made `makeParser` resolve a lazily-built regex.
- `A`/`a` now use those; the default path is case-insensitive like moment's `meridiemParse` (so `'pm'` parses with the `A` token too).

Verified against moment for `ja` (午前/午後), `zh-cn` (上午/下午), `br` (a.m./g.m.) and `en` (AM/am/PM/pm) — all now equal moment's `valueOf()`. Full suite 524/524 green (plus my temporary probe, since deleted); eslint clean.

Fixed. `src/plugin/duration/index.js`: the `unitToMS` table had no `milliseconds` key, but the plugin normalizes every unit through `prettyUnit = unit => `${$u.p(unit)}s``, so `'milliseconds'`, `'millisecond'` and `'ms'` all resolve to `'milliseconds'`. The two-argument path `wrapper(input * unitToMS[prettyUnit(unit)], this)` therefore computed `input * undefined` → `NaN`, so `dayjs.duration(1234, 'milliseconds')` gave `asMilliseconds() === NaN` and `toISOString() === 'P0D'` (also broke `.add(500, 'milliseconds')`). The plain-number and object paths happened to work via the `|| 1` fallback.

Change (one line): added `milliseconds: 1` to `unitToMS`.

Verified: `dayjs.duration(n)` and `dayjs.duration(1234, 'milliseconds'|'millisecond'|'ms')` now match `moment.duration` for `asMilliseconds()`, `milliseconds()`, `seconds()`, `toISOString()` and `.add(500,'milliseconds')`. Full suite 524/524 green, eslint clean, no test files touched.
